title: Apple India Crosses Rs 1 Lakh Crore in Revenue as Profit Jumps 66%
excerpt: FY26 operating revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,03,853 crore and net profit to Rs 5,311 crore, as iPhone volumes grew 24% in a smartphone market that managed just 2%.
body:
• Apple India's operating revenue crossed Rs 1 lakh crore for the first time in FY26, rising 31% to Rs 1,03,853 crore, while net profit jumped 66% to Rs 5,311 crore.
  • Profit grew twice as fast as sales, lifting Apple's net margin to 5.1% from 4% a year earlier, according to Registrar of Companies filings reported by Inc42.
  • iPhone volumes in India rose 24% in FY26, more than double the prior year's pace, in a smartphone market that grew just 2% by volume.
  • Apple's India sales revenue of Rs 1,03,853 crore now sits close to Samsung Electronics India's Rs 1.12 lakh crore, though Samsung's figure covers TVs, appliances and network gear as well as phones.

Apple's India business has crossed a threshold no one would have predicted a decade ago. Revenue from operations rose 31% to Rs 1,03,853 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, the first time Apple India has passed Rs 1 lakh crore, and net profit rose 66% to Rs 5,311 crore, according to filings with the Registrar of Companies accessed through AltInfo and reported by Inc42.

The acceleration is the story inside the headline. In FY25, revenue had grown 18% and profit 16%. In FY26 both rates roughly doubled, and profit grew at twice the pace of sales, which means Apple is not just selling more in India. It is keeping more of each rupee.

Where the Money Came From

Sales of traded goods, iPhones, Macs, iPads and other products, jumped about 33% to Rs 99,068 crore from Rs 74,680 crore. Services added the rest: support services including AppleCare grew 7.6% to Rs 4,292.8 crore, and maintenance contracts brought in Rs 492.4 crore. Total expenses rose 28% to Rs 96,224 crore.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1Q1ym8uHRP8

The market underneath explains the mix. India's smartphone market grew just 2% by volume and 9% by value in FY26, according to Counterpoint Research. The premium segment, phones priced above Rs 30,000, grew 12% by volume, and Apple's iPhone volumes rose 24%, up from 11% growth the year before, Angel One reported. Apple is winning the only part of the market that is expanding quickly.

The Samsung Comparison, With a Caveat

Apple India's revenue now approaches Samsung Electronics India's Rs 1.12 lakh crore for FY26. The comparison flatters neither side cleanly: Samsung's total covers televisions, home appliances, telecom equipment and exports, while its mobile phone revenue alone was Rs 81,472 crore, down 1.4%. On phones, the product line Apple sells, Apple is now the larger business in India by reported sales.

One more boundary matters. Apple India's books do not include the full value of iPhones made in India for export, which sit with contract manufacturers Foxconn and Tata Electronics. iPhone exports from India crossed Rs 2 lakh crore in FY26, a manufacturing figure larger than Apple's entire domestic sales operation.

What It Means

India has moved from a rounding error in Apple's global accounts to a business with the revenue of a mid-sized Indian listed company, growing at 31% in a flat market. For investors, the FY26 filings confirm the premiumisation trade in Indian consumer tech is not a narrative. It is in the audited numbers, and Apple is its largest single beneficiary.

What's Next

The test for FY27 is whether volume growth holds as Apple widens its retail and manufacturing footprint, and whether services, still a small share of the total, can compound into a second engine. The June quarter already delivered strong double-digit India growth, aided by demand for the more affordable MacBook Neo.
